title: 3.2. Loops in Python: while and for
summary: Automate repetitive tasks with while and for loops, iterate with range(), and control loop execution using break, continue, and loop-else clauses.
learningObjectives: Construct while loops with terminating conditions to prevent infinite loops.
Use for loops with range(start, stop, step) to iterate through sequences.
Apply break to exit prematurely, continue to skip the current iteration, and understand the loop-else block.

sections.heading: 3.2.1 The while Loop & Preventing Infinite Loops
sections.content: A while loop repeatedly executes an indented block as long as its condition remains True. The loop body must modify at least one variable involved in the condition to avoid an infinite loop.

sections.heading: 3.2.2 The for Loop and the range() Generator
sections.content:
The for loop is designed to iterate through sequences. Combined with the built-in range() function, it provides a clean counter mechanism:
• range(stop): Generates values from 0 up to (but NOT including) stop.
• range(start, stop): Generates values from start up to stop - 1.
• range(start, stop, step): Steps by step (can be negative for reverse counting).

knowledgeChecks.prompt: What numbers are generated by list(range(2, 8, 2))?
knowledgeChecks.explanation: range(start, stop, step) stops strictly before the stop value (8), yielding 2, 4, and 6.

recap: while loops repeat while a condition holds; for loops traverse sequences; range() produces arithmetic progressions.
